papers.title: Atomic structure and dynamics of the mechanosensitive channel MscL from Escherichia coli by cryo-EM and solid-state NMR.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of E. coli MscL in nanodiscs captured a closed conformation, while solid-state NMR of the low-threshold G22S mutant in liposomes revealed widespread conformational changes indicating early opening transitions. Combining both methods shows lipid-protein interactions are key determinants of gating, providing a framework for studying mechanosensitive channel dynamics and designing channels with tunable gating.

papers.title: Rapid protamine evolution suppresses meiotic drive in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Using in vivo gene replacement in Drosophila, the authors show the rapidly evolving protamine Mst77F protects the X chromosome from a killer-target meiotic drive system in a dosage- and sequence-dependent manner. Divergent orthologs or reduced dosage caused X-bearing sperm DNA compaction defects and male-biased progeny, indicating meiotic drive suppression drives rapid protamine evolution.

papers.title: Translocation-induced enhancer rewiring reveals cryptic oncogenic circuits in multiple myeloma.
papers.summary: Transfinder, a multiomic pipeline combining long-read sequencing, Hi-C, ChIP-seq/CUT&Tag and RNA-seq, deconvolves enhancer-promoter neo-loops at translocation breakpoints. In multiple myeloma it identified novel translocations activating MYC and CBX7, and detected enhancer hijacking in CML and pancreatic cancer, linking 3D genome architecture to actionable oncogenic dependencies.

papers.title: A biohybrid mesh harvester for distributed energy harvesting in living tissues.
papers.summary: The authors built a biohybrid mesh energy harvester embedding individual harvesting units within a tissue-mimicking network, demonstrated in in vitro cardiac tissue. This distributed architecture achieved energy density over an order of magnitude higher than centralized substrate-based approaches, offering a generalizable framework for powering bio-integrated electronics and future in vivo biohybrid systems.

papers.title: Real-time single-molecule imaging in zebrafish embryos uncovers noncanonical translation.
papers.summary: Using ALFA-based nascent chain labeling with lattice light-sheet microscopy in zebrafish embryos, the authors visualized bmp2b translation at single-molecule resolution in real time. Only a subset of mRNAs were actively translated, and translation operated below maximal initiation. The bmp2b 5'UTR also supported cap-independent translation, providing a quantitative framework for in vivo translation kinetics.

papers.title: Clonal lineage tracing and parallel multiomics profiling reveal transcriptional heterogeneity induced by ARID1A deficiency.
papers.summary: Combining lineage tracing with single-cell multiomics, the authors tracked ARID1A loss in individual clones. Deficiency increased transcriptional variability within and across clones, broadened chromatin accessibility, and depended on residual SMARCA4. Variability-rich clones showed no growth advantage normally but were preferentially recovered under stress and lung colonization, consistent with bet-hedging in tumor evolution.

papers.title: Self-buoyant cell-spheroid culture programming multi-spheroid assembly.
papers.summary: The authors present a self-buoyant spheroid culture where microbubbles lift cell-adhesive droplets, enabling field-free one-drop-one-spheroid arrays. Droplet 'kiss' transfer moves spheroids in about one second, allowing parallel media exchange and drug dosing, plus programmable multi-spheroid assembly and fusion into 'buoyantoid' patterns, supporting scalable assembloid engineering and high-throughput screening.

papers.title: Human trilayer engineered blood vessel reveals influence of fibroblasts on disease progression in model of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria.
papers.summary: A trilayer tissue-engineered blood vessel containing smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts modeled Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome. HGPS fibroblasts elevated vascular pathology features, and base-editing correction returned them to healthy levels. Fibroblasts drove ECM dysregulation and fibrotic signaling, clarifying their underappreciated role in vascular disease progression and therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco.
papers.summary: The authors applied the structure-informed ML model ESM-IF1 to design a directed evolution library for tobacco Rubisco large subunit, selected in Rubisco-dependent E. coli. Enriched variants improved catalytic efficiency, including T39I boosting carboxylation rate 29% and efficiency 43%. Several changes lie outside natural plant lineages, showing ML-assisted design explores functional sequence space beyond natural diversity.

papers.title: Targeted integration of extrachromosomal arrays in C. elegans using PhiC31 integrase.
papers.summary: PhiAT uses PhiC31 integrase to integrate C. elegans extrachromosomal arrays into attB sites nonmutagenically and efficiently, on three chromosomes or, with co-injected Cas9 and an attB repair template, at arbitrary genomic sites. Single injections integrated 1-18 megabase arrays, including one strain carrying 65% of the yeast genome, replacing unstable arrays with targeted transgenes.

papers.title: Cis-regulatory inactivation of vitamin D signaling confers extreme calcium tolerance in Jialing fish.
papers.summary: Jialing fish in China's high-calcium karst lakes evolved extreme calcium tolerance through cis-regulatory loss of vitamin D signaling: a VDRB enhancer mutation suppresses VDRB and its downstream calcium transporter Calb2a by over 90%. Zebrafish knockouts of either gene survived hypercalcemia better, showing regulatory dismantling of an endocrine pathway driving ecological adaptation.

papers.title: Endogenous retrovirus control of calbindin is essential for human early embryogenesis.
papers.summary: A HERVH endogenous retrovirus integration on chromosome 8q21.3, acquired during homininae evolution, drives chimeric HERVH-CALB1 expression in human preimplantation embryos and embryonic stem cells. CALB1 expression is critical for ESC growth, senescence prevention, and blastoid formation, suggesting the same cis-regulatory co-option observed in lung cancer echoes an essential developmental function.

papers.title: Epigenetic insights into extreme longevity in the world's oldest terrestrial animal, Jonathan.
papers.summary: The authors sequenced the genome and methylome of Jonathan, a 194-year-old Aldabra giant tortoise, comparing him to other tortoises and younger Aldabras. Lower-entropy methylome regions were enriched for promoters of mitochondrial electron transport chain and RNA metabolism genes, supporting a model where low methylation entropy maintains efficient energy production, RNA processing, and genomic repair in long-lived species.

papers.title: Herpes simplex virus pUL56 abolishes neuronal activity by removing voltage-gated ion channels from the plasma membrane.
papers.summary: Mapping HSV-1 infection in human iPSC-derived neurons across the lytic cycle, the authors found extensive plasma membrane remodeling removing voltage-gated sodium, potassium, and calcium channels, abolishing synchronous calcium signaling. The viral ubiquitin-ligase adaptor pUL56 is the principal effector: degrading ion channels depends on its E3-ligase-binding motifs, and pUL56 expression alone abolishes neuronal activity.

papers.title: HIF-1α-driven lactate from mesenchymal stem/stromal cells reprograms monocyte metabolism and suppresses autoimmune uveoretinitis.
papers.summary: Mesenchymal stromal cells produce lactate in a HIF-1alpha-dependent manner, which reprograms monocyte metabolism, suppresses glycolytic activation, and redirects differentiation toward an immunosuppressive phenotype. Blocking lactate production with oxamate or HIF1A knockdown reduced therapeutic efficacy in autoimmune uveoretinitis, identifying the HIF-1alpha-lactate axis as a targetable pathway for optimizing MSC therapies.

papers.title: A developmentally restricted γδ T cell-IL-17A axis supports mouse heart regeneration.
papers.summary: Following cardiac injury in neonatal mice, a distinct gamma-delta T cell population absent from older non-regenerative hearts accumulates and rapidly produces IL-17A. Ablating these cells or disrupting IL-17 signaling impaired heart regeneration and cardiac function. IL-17A acts on myeloid cells to enable apoptotic cell clearance while limiting sustained inflammation, defining a developmentally restricted regenerative immune axis.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics reveals the heterogeneous landscape of innate lymphoid cells in zebrafish.
papers.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq in zebrafish reveals broad innate lymphoid cell diversity, including mammalian-like conventional subsets and unconventional ILC-like populations with distinct tissue distributions. The full ILC repertoire emerges early, independent of hematopoietic stem cells, then persists via an HSC-dependent mechanism. IL-2 receptor beta is essential for ILC-mediated immunity, illuminating vertebrate innate immune evolution.

papers.title: Quantifying the energetic costs and growth benefits of phagocytosis.
papers.summary: The authors built a mathematical model integrating prey capture, engulfment, and digestion to quantify when primitive phagocytosis benefits a cell relative to a non-phagocytosing ancestor. Phagocytosis outperforms the ancestor across many conditions, with engulfment rate delineating advantage, and remains beneficial even without vacuole recycling, suggesting plausible evolutionary waypoints toward eukaryotic endomembrane systems.

papers.title: Multicancer analysis reveals mtDNA copy number as a key determinant of mutational load and cancer progression.
papers.summary: Analyzing whole-genome data across cancer types, the authors show mtDNA copy number increases with mutational load and bears a signature of compensating for mitochondrial dysfunction. Low-mtDNA samples show increased expression of cancer-promoting genes involved in migration and EMT. The findings link mitochondrial functional state to mutational burden and cancer progression.

papers.title: TEAD4 Regulates apical domain homeostasis and cell-positioning to maintain the trophectoderm lineage during mouse blastocyst development.
papers.summary: TEAD4, known for trophectoderm specification, also maintains trophectoderm integrity during blastocyst maturation. Knockdown disrupted outer cell apical domains, causing clones to misallocate into the inner cell mass via migration or repositioning. TEAD4 regulates actin and adhesion genes, and combined knockdown of targets Rnd1/Rnd3 partially rescued allocation, showing TEAD4 actively preserves lineage positioning.

papers.title: The MICAL family at the Rho-Rab interface: coordinating actin dynamics through oxidation and scaffolding.
papers.summary: This review highlights the MICAL monooxygenase family, especially MICAL1, as connectors between Rho and Rab GTPase signaling and actin cytoskeleton regulation through oxidation and scaffolding. It discusses how dysregulated actin dynamics contribute to neurodevelopmental, neurodegenerative, and cancer phenotypes, and positions MICALs as potential therapeutic targets at the Rho-Rab interface.

papers.title: Netrin-1 and UNC5H receptors: role in cell fate determination and carcinogenesis.
papers.summary: This review covers UNC5H dependence receptors, which promote survival when bound by Netrin-1 and trigger apoptosis via DAPK and PP2A when unbound. UNC5H downregulation and Netrin-1 upregulation in tumors promote survival, and targeting this axis induces cancer cell death, reverses EMT, and inhibits metastasis, with current therapeutic strategies under clinical testing.

papers.title: KDM2B controls HIF levels and activity through its JmjC and CxxC domains.
papers.summary: KDM2B regulates HIF-1alpha in a cell-type-dependent manner: depletion decreased HIF activity in U2OS and MDA-MB-231 cells but increased it in HeLa. KDM2B requires its JmjC demethylase and CxxC domains, supports RNA polymerase II recruitment to HIF1A promoter, and promotes proliferation under hypoxia, establishing KDM2B as a regulator of hypoxic adaptation.

papers.title: Graph-based representations in modern protein science.
papers.summary: This review traces graph-based representations in protein science: residue interaction networks for structure, genotype networks for evolution, and protein-protein interaction graphs for cellular function. It follows development from early topology through statistical coupling to machine-learning-driven geometric representations, emphasizing graphs complement, rather than replace, sequences and multiple sequence alignments.

papers.title: SF3B4 'reads' RNA that is methylated by METTL16.
papers.summary: Screening an RNA-binding domain array for m6A effectors identified spliceosomal protein SF3B4 as an m6A reader. RIP-seq showed SF3B4 prefers the GRAGRA motif recognized by METTL16, with shared targets including BCR and MET oncogene transcripts. SF3B4 thus participates in RNA metabolism downstream of METTL16-mediated methylation.

papers.title: The non-canonical CDK2 activator SPY1 uses separable mechanisms to activate phosphorylated and unphosphorylated CDK2.
papers.summary: SPY1, a non-canonical CDK2 activator, activates both phosphorylated and unphosphorylated CDK2 as effectively as cyclin A. FRET showed SPY1 induces cyclin-A-like conformational shifts regardless of phosphorylation state. The D136A mutant, inactive on unphosphorylated CDK2, still activates phosphorylated CDK2, demonstrating separable activation mechanisms with implications for inhibitor binding.

papers.title: Bisecting GlcNAc in N-glycan regulates synaptic maturation.
papers.summary: Mgat3 knockout mice, lacking bisecting GlcNAc in N-glycans, showed impaired neurite extension, reduced spine maturation, and diminished stimulus-evoked neuronal activity. AMPA receptor glycoproteins accumulated less in postsynaptic density membranes and interacted weakly with TMARP8. Bisecting GlcNAc thus regulates synaptic maturation through glycoprotein trafficking, revealing a new glycan-based mechanism of neuronal regulation.

papers.title: Loss of O-GlcNAc transferase activity impairs the dynamic formation of protective stress granules in ischemic cardiomyocytes.
papers.summary: In cardiomyocytes, O-GlcNAc transferase is required for efficient stress granule formation during arsenite stress and ischemia/reperfusion. G3BP1 T268 was identified as an O-GlcNAc site functionally important for stress granule assembly. OGT knockdown reduced stress granule formation in primary cardiomyocytes and hearts during ischemia, implicating O-GlcNAc-dependent condensate dynamics in cardioprotection.

papers.title: Substrate-specific regulation of the mTORC1 pathway by G protein-coupled receptors.
papers.summary: Muscarinic receptor M5R regulates mTORC1 substrates differentially: it promoted S6K1 and 4EBP1 phosphorylation while triggering TFEB dephosphorylation, thereby stimulating protein synthesis without inhibiting lysosome biogenesis. The study demonstrates substrate-specific mTORC1 control by GPCRs, with implications for evaluating GPCR ligands as therapeutic agents targeting mTORC1.

papers.title: Heat stress promotes GTBP-1 association with perinuclear P-bodies in the C. elegans germline.
papers.summary: The C. elegans G3BP1 homolog GTBP-1 forms germline granules during heat stress, with NTF2 domain required for granule enrichment and IDR, RRM, and RGG domains controlling dynamics. GTBP-1 granules strongly associate with P-bodies, and loss of mTOR effector RSks-1 suppresses fertility defects, linking stress granules to temperature-dependent reproductive homeostasis.

papers.title: The dynamics of gene copy-number mutations: transient changes with long-lasting consequences.
papers.summary: This review reframes bacterial gene copy-number mutations as non-neutral: tandem duplications arise orders of magnitude more often than SNPs and collapse even faster, transiently increasing gene dosage. Duplications slow divergence, act with purifying selection as conservation forces, and enable bet-hedging, emphasizing structural variation analysis for understanding bacterial evolution and pathogen emergence.

papers.title: Insulin-stimulated phosphorylation of CLASP2 by ERK regulates microtubule plus-end binding of CLASP2 and insulin-regulated microtubule stabilization.
papers.summary: Insulin stimulates ERK-mediated phosphorylation of CLASP2 at multiple proline-directed serines in 3T3-L1 adipocytes. A penta-alanine mutant showed diminished microtubule plus-end trailing and reduced insulin-induced microtubule stabilization. CLASP2 protein was decreased in insulin-resistant mouse adipose tissue, positioning ERK-dependent CLASP2 phosphorylation as a contributor to insulin-regulated microtubule stabilization.

papers.title: A distinct interphase microtubule state marks host cell permissiveness to Chlamydia pneumoniae entry.
papers.summary: Using Chlamydia pneumoniae, the authors show that host cell microtubule state determines bacterial entry permissiveness: acetylated microtubule-enriched cells were preferentially infected, while Taxol enhanced and tubacin-induced acetylation alone did not, pointing to a permissive state of stabilized long-lived microtubules. Infection reciprocally increased acetylation, and chlamydial Tarp-family protein CPn0572 promotes microtubule persistence.

papers.title: A truncated form of the cGMP-gated cation channel β-subunit lacking the GARP2 region transiently restores rod structure and function.
papers.summary: Transgenic mice expressing a truncated cGMP-gated channel beta-subunit lacking GARP2 on a CNGB1-null background showed normal disc morphology and membrane connections up to 6 months with function comparable to wild type until 7.5 months, but progressive degeneration followed. Long-term rod survival requires the N-terminal extension, while early structural defects cannot be attributed to GARP loss.

papers.title: Average local nucleosome motion remains nearly constant during interphase in living human cells.
papers.summary: Combining single-nucleosome imaging with FUCCI cell-cycle probes in asynchronous human cells, the authors found local nucleosome motion remains nearly constant throughout interphase, including euchromatin-enriched H3.3 nucleosomes. Transcription inhibition, replication stress, or DNA damage increased motion, suggesting constitutive chromatin mobility supports housekeeping functions while cells transiently mobilize chromatin for ad hoc tasks.

papers.title: The transcription factor CLAMP is required for neurogenesis in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: The Drosophila transcription factor CLAMP promotes neural stem cell proliferation and glial niche production while repressing neurogenic genes, particularly in the optic lobe. CLAMP directly binds Notch and Tailless, master regulators of brain development. Loss of CLAMP severely disrupts optic lobe development, linking a chromatin adaptor to stemness and niche signaling.

papers.title: Cell adhesion molecules CadN, DIP-α, and klg regulate axon targeting and dendritic elaboration through synergistic and opposing effects.
papers.summary: In Drosophila dm12 amacrine neurons, N-cadherin and DIP-alpha cooperate in parallel to promote axon targeting and dendritic elaboration, while Klingon levels are homeostatically tuned: both loss and overexpression expand dendritic coverage. Dendritic expansion via klg manipulation suppressed axon mistargeting in cadN and DIP-alpha mutants, revealing integrated adhesion molecule control of neural wiring.

papers.title: Autophagy, the ubiquitin proteasome system, and the MAPK pathway control the temperature dependence of synaptic growth.
papers.summary: Using the Drosophila larval neuromuscular junction, the authors show rearing temperature drives synaptic growth in phasic but not tonic motor neurons. Autophagy activity changes with temperature, and autophagy genes regulate this growth through Highwire and a MAPK pathway involving Wallenda and p38b, revealing genetic pathways controlling temperature-dependent synaptic plasticity.

papers.title: An essential role of the AMPK-related kinase snrk in regulating Drosophila sleep.
papers.summary: SNRK, an AMPK-related kinase, is essential for Drosophila sleep: knockout caused profound night-time sleep loss exceeding the known SIK3 phenotype, rescued by neuronal expression. SNRK functions in sleep-inhibiting cholinergic neurons, and pharmacological blockade of nicotinic acetylcholine receptors rescued the sleep loss, establishing SNRK as a fundamental sleep regulator.

papers.title: Systems genetics analysis reveals immune mediators of coronavirus disease severity in mice.
papers.summary: Systems genetics in Collaborative Cross mice identified immune predictors of coronavirus disease severity, extensive genetic regulation of immune responses at homeostasis and during infection, and causal pathways linking host loci, immune traits, and outcomes through Bayesian mediation. Immune effects on severity were largely consistent across viruses, while mediating immune traits were mostly virus-dependent.

papers.title: A glycolysis-calcineurin regulatory axis orchestrates titan cell formation in Cryptococcus neoformans.
papers.summary: In Cryptococcus neoformans, glycolysis is critical for titan cell formation, a virulence trait promoting immune evasion. Glycolytic disruption impaired titanization, rescued by exogenous cAMP, acting through a calcineurin-dependent axis: calcineurin inhibitors reduced titan cell formation, calcium supplementation rescued the Hxk2-deficient defect, and intracellular calcium dynamics were involved in this morphological transition.

papers.title: The impact of P-element-induced hybrid dysgenesis on the male germline in Drosophila simulans.
papers.summary: P-element hybrid dysgenesis in male Drosophila simulans elevates transposition with insertion preference near replication origins, increases P-element expression, reduces splicing suppression, and depletes mature sperm. Fertility assays showed high male sterility rates but otherwise modest fertility effects. The piRNA pathway functions in testes, suggesting P-elements may spread more readily through males.

papers.title: QTL mapping.
papers.summary: This primer introduces quantitative trait locus (QTL) mapping for readers with limited statistical background: how DNA markers segregating according to Mendelian expectations are combined with quantitative trait inheritance to locate genomic regions influencing traits, covering crossing designs in plants and structured family data in animals and humans, and factors determining QTL interval resolution.

papers.title: Conservation and divergence within the Arabidopsis TPL/TPR corepressor family.
papers.summary: Analysis of the Arabidopsis TPL/TPR corepressor family shows TPL, TPR1, and TPR4 are primary repressors for most pathways including flowering, immunity, and auxin responses, while TPR2 and TPR3 play lesser or opposite roles. Natural variation in the EAR-binding pocket defines three subtypes, and cell-type-specific effector expression enabled tuning root architecture, suggesting engineering potential.

papers.title: Ataxin-2 regulates the synaptonemal complex to ensure chromosome pairing during female meiosis.
papers.summary: The RNA-binding protein Ataxin-2 positively regulates meiotic factors, especially synaptonemal complex components, in Drosophila female meiosis. Depletion reduced SC mRNA and protein, causing defective SC assembly and maintenance, failure of homologous chromosome pairing, and aneuploidy risk. ATX2 thus coordinates a post-transcriptional layer essential for meiotic chromosome segregation and fertility.

papers.title: A hybrid transcriptome assembly reveals coding and noncoding landscapes in Drosophila hemocytes.
papers.summary: Combining Oxford Nanopore long-read with Illumina short-read sequencing in Drosophila hemocytes uncovered full-length transcripts with novel boundaries and 349 previously unannotated long noncoding RNAs induced during wasp infestation. Two highly induced lncRNAs marked lamellocytes and crystal cells, and RNAi depletion of two impaired lamellocyte formation, demonstrating functional lncRNA roles in innate immunity.

papers.title: The Drosophila SWI/SNF complex subunit Bap60 is required for training-induced gene transcription during long-term memory formation.
papers.summary: The SWI/SNF subunit Bap60 is required in the adult Drosophila mushroom body for long-term memory and training-induced transcription. Bap60-regulated BRM-bound genes are enriched for SR binding sites, with Prospero identified as a key downstream transcription factor whose knockdown also impairs memory. Bap60 thus regulates memory gene induction downstream of or cooperating with immediate early genes.

papers.title: A genetic model of copulatory wounding in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: Overexpressing the serine protease Hayan in Drosophila induces copulatory wounding, marked by melanin deposits on the female abdomen from male mid-leg abrasion. Wounds heal through enlarged polyploid cells arising by cell fusion for small injuries or endocycling for larger ones, providing a genetic model for mating injury repair and wound-induced polyploidization.

papers.title: Ribosome-associated chaperones integrate co-translational mitochondrial protein import, stress signaling, and proteostasis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.summary: In yeast, ribosome-associated chaperones NAC and SSB1/2 have distinct roles in mitochondrial protein import: NAC loss activates retrograde metabolic adaptation without respiratory defects, while SSB1/2 loss disrupts proteostasis, TORC1 signaling, autophagy, and mitophagy. SSB1/2 supports co-translational import and ribosome-mitochondria association, defining an integrated network linking translation to mitochondrial homeostasis.

papers.title: Identification of a "new" crystal/Su(Ste) locus on the Drosophila melanogaster Y chromosome, resembling a piRNA cluster regulating Stellate repeats and transposons.
papers.summary: Comprehensive annotation of the Drosophila Y chromosome crystal/Su(Ste) repeats identified a novel disorganized locus with piRNA cluster features regulating Stellate repeats and transposons, plus four additional heterochromatic Su(Ste)-like loci absent from release 6. Two new repeat types carrying Heta and Gypsy12 fragments refine the Y chromosome map and the crystal-Stellate piRNA system.

papers.title: Sperm entry without genome inheritance: incorporate or exclude-egg-intrinsic control of paternal genome fate in Cobitis fish.
papers.summary: Using time-resolved imaging of over 1,300 Cobitis fish embryos across sexual, hybrid, and heterogeneric crosses, the authors captured two postfertilization outcomes: eggs incorporate paternal genomes with centrosome licensing and chromatin acetylation, or exclude them with failed centrosome licensing and multiple ectopic asters. Paternal genome fate is thus determined by egg-intrinsic mechanisms linking centrosomes to chromatin remodeling.

papers.title: microRNAs affecting development of body pigmentation in adult Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.summary: Gain- and loss-of-function screens identified 48 Drosophila microRNAs sufficient and 22 necessary for adult body pigmentation. For microRNAs with opposing effects in both screens, computational targets included 93 known pigmentation genes. Mir-8 regulates three pigmentation genes through their 3'UTRs, showing microRNAs coordinately regulate pigmentation development and potentially pigmentation divergence.

papers.title: Effect of population structure and stabilizing selection on quantitative genetic variation.
papers.summary: Using analytical approximations and simulations of subdivided populations under stabilizing selection, the authors identify a critical migration threshold below which population structure strongly inflates genic variance. Variation within subpopulations peaks near this threshold, genetic bases are most similar across subpopulations there, and a diffusion-based mean-field approach accurately predicts variance components, with implications for GWAS portability.

papers.title: Cryptic peroxisomal targeting determinants in protistan glycolytic enzymes suggest a "how" for glycosome evolution.
papers.summary: In Naegleria gruberi, cryptic peroxisomal targeting signals arise in metabolic enzymes via stop-codon readthrough or alternative splicing, are conserved in N. fowleri, and function in trypanosomatid glycosome import. Similar signals appear across diverse protists, suggesting dual protein localization diversified peroxisome function early in eukaryotic evolution and provides a plausible mechanism for glycosome evolution.

papers.title: Inherited long telomeres induce a genome-wide transcriptional response in budding yeast.
papers.summary: Budding yeast strains inheriting long telomeres show a distinct genome-wide transcriptional profile, upregulating membrane transporters and downregulating a smaller gene set distributed across chromosomes. Affected genes are enriched for Rap1 binding sites, consistent with long telomeres sequestering Rap1 and altering transcription at non-telomeric sites, with changes scaling with telomere length across generations.

papers.title: High prevalence of Plasmodium ovalewallikeri in co-infections with Plasmodium falciparum in symptomatic than asymptomatic Plasmodium parasite infections in Kisumu, Kenya.
papers.summary: qPCR analysis of 741 samples from Kisumu, Kenya found P. falciparum in 88.3% and P. ovalewallikeri in 20.6% of infections. P. falciparum and P. ovalewallikeri were significantly more prevalent in symptomatic cases, while P. malariae and P. ovalecurtisi predominated in asymptomatic infections, indicating species composition influences clinical presentation in co-endemic settings.

papers.title: Spatial and genetic dynamics of Plasmodium falciparum histidine-rich protein2 in sub-Saharan Africa.
papers.summary: Analyzing 215 pfhrp2 sequences from sub-Saharan Africa, the authors found extensive insertion-deletion variation across about 10 repeat motif types, with types 2, 4, and 7 most prevalent. Baker model predictions indicate most isolates remain detectable by mRDT monoclonal antibodies. High diversity with very low differentiation suggests gene flow, with biological fitness dominating over diagnostic evasion.

papers.title: Neurological tissue dissection techniques in mouse models for reproducible scientific results: Brain, spinal cord, cerebrospinal fluid, and sciatic nerve.
papers.summary: This protocol paper presents five standardized mouse neurological tissue procedures: brain extraction, brain microdissection, spinal cord extrusion, cerebrospinal fluid collection, and sciatic nerve dissection. Each was refined through transcriptomics and pharmaceutical research applications, performed under BSL-2 guidelines with defined materials lists, designed to minimize tissue damage and improve dissection accuracy and reproducibility.

papers.title: Computational identification of natural CXCR4-binding candidates relevant to endometriosis and ovarian cancer progression.
papers.summary: Computational screening of 18 phytochemicals against reconstructed human CXCR4 identified naringenin as the top binder, with favorable docking exceeding apigenin and the co-crystallized ligand IT1T. Two independent 100-ns membrane-embedded simulations confirmed consistent structural behavior, and MM/GBSA estimates were most favorable for naringenin, though the authors note predicted favorable binding requires experimental toxicological validation.

papers.title: Macrophages discriminate and sort pathogenic bacteria and apoptotic material during dual-target phagocytosis.
papers.summary: Using quantitative confocal and live-cell imaging, the authors show macrophages handle dual targets differently: apoptotic cells alone are engulfed intact within tight actin-rich cups, while bacteria-laden apoptotic cells trigger protrusive extensions that selectively extract individual bacteria along the apoptotic scaffold. Most phagosomes contain single cargo types, demonstrating macrophages discriminate and sort complex targets during uptake.

papers.title: Impaired fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial injury mediated by the AMPK/PPARα pathway: A key mechanism in high-fat diet-aggravated ulcerative colitis.
papers.summary: In a mouse model combining high-fat diet with DSS colitis, HFD exacerbated disease through lipid accumulation and microbiota dysbiosis triggering oxidative stress and AMPK suppression. AMPK inactivation downregulated PPAR-alpha and fatty acid oxidation enzymes CPT1A and ACOX1, worsening lipotoxicity and mitochondrial damage. The AMPK agonist AICAR provided support for this pathway's therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Investigating the anticancer potential of phytochemicals from the mangrove Rhizophora mucronata as inhibitors of lung cancer-associated proteins: Insights from multiscale computational and in silico analyses.
papers.summary: A multiscale computational pipeline screened 14 Rhizophora mucronata phytochemicals against KEAP1 Kelch and YEATS2 YEATS domains involved in lung cancer. Ligand L10 (cyclohexane-1,2,3,4,5,6-hexaol) showed the smallest HOMO-LUMO gap, favorable binding to KEAP1, multiple hydrogen bonds, and stable 100-ns molecular dynamics, suggesting potential as a low-toxicity NSCLC therapeutic lead.

papers.title: Lysosomal Expansion Compartments Mediate Zinc and Copper Homeostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.summary: In C. elegans intestinal cells, lysosomes expand in response to excess zinc, copper, manganese, and cadmium, with lysosome-number mutants hypersensitive to copper and manganese toxicity. X-ray fluorescence microscopy confirmed metals accumulate in lysosomal lumens, and copper transporter CUA-1.1 localizes to expansion compartments, indicating a general lysosome-based metal storage mechanism across multiple metals.

papers.title: Tumor-derived DLK1 restrains tumor progression through remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment.
papers.summary: Tumor-derived DLK1, a non-canonical Notch ligand, declines during tumor progression partly through hypoxia-responsive miR-338-5p. Ectopic DLK1 suppressed B16 melanoma and LLC1 carcinoma growth through immune remodeling: increased T cell infiltration, reduced myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and macrophage activation. Recombinant DLK1-Fc directly enhanced macrophage activation, identifying DLK1 loss as a driver of immunosuppression.

papers.title: From heteroplasmy shift to direct base correction: mitochondrial genome editing for disease modeling and therapy.
papers.summary: This review organizes mitochondrial genome editing strategies from selective mutant genome depletion to direct base correction, covering mitoTALENs, mitoZFNs, mitoArcus, DddA-derived cytosine base editors, and strand-selective editors. It discusses applications to heteroplasmy shifting, disease modeling, and addressing tissue-specific pathogenic thresholds in mitochondrial genetic diseases with neurological, muscular, cardiac, and visual phenotypes.

papers.title: Viburnum opulus protects against acetaminophen-induced splenic injury through coordinated antioxidant and anti-inflammatory responses.
papers.summary: In rats, prophylactic Viburnum opulus protected against acetaminophen-induced splenic injury, attenuating histomorphological disruption and normalizing cleaved caspase-3, NF-kappaB, iNOS, Ki-67, SOD1, and NRF2 expression. Network pharmacology identified 44 shared targets between major constituents and apap-toxicity genes, with AKT1, NFKB1, PTGS2, and STAT3 as key hubs underlying coordinated antioxidant and anti-inflammatory protection.

papers.title: Unravelling the synergy of curcumin and quercetin in the adipogenesis pathway: highlighting molecular dynamics and epigenetic reversibility.
papers.summary: Combining molecular docking, MD simulation, and 3T3-L1 adipocyte validation, the authors examined curcumin and quercetin against obesity targets GLP1R, PPARG, and LEPR. Quercetin enhanced GLP1R and LEPR compactness and stability while curcumin maintained PPARG conformation, and combination treatment showed synergistic effects, supporting their potential as complementary anti-obesity agents with epigenetic reversibility implications.

papers.title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles modulate Th1- and STAT1-Associated inflammatory responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients with osteoarthritis.
papers.summary: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles reduced CD4+IFN-gamma+ Th1 cell frequency in both healthy and osteoarthritis patient PBMCs, decreasing from 33.8% to 26.9% in OA samples. Vesicles modulated STAT1-associated inflammatory signaling and reduced IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha expression, supporting their potential as cell-free immunomodulatory therapeutics for osteoarthritis.

papers.title: Mitochondrial dysfunction of renal tubular epithelial cells in chronic kidney disease-associated fibrosis: from organelle homeostasis to multicellular remodeling.
papers.summary: This review organizes renal tubular epithelial cell mitochondrial dysfunction in chronic kidney disease fibrosis within a tubule-to-niche framework, distinguishing causal perturbation from association. Persistent mitochondrial injury suppresses fatty acid oxidation, increases reactive oxygen species, destabilizes mtDNA, and disrupts mitophagy, promoting maladaptive repair and paracrine fibrotic signaling, and is treated as a context-dependent amplifier rather than universal initiator.

papers.title: RRP12 knockdown inhibited inflammation and p53/NF-κB pathway and alleviated heterotopic ossification in mice.
papers.summary: In mice, RRP12 expression was upregulated during heterotopic ossification, and knockdown retarded progression, alleviated inflammation, and inactivated the p53/NF-kappaB pathway. In bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, RRP12 suppression reduced osteogenic differentiation, identifying RRP12 as a potential therapeutic target, though upstream regulators and translational feasibility require further study.

papers.title: Sinensetin ameliorates osteoarthritis progression by modulating the NF-κB/NLRP3 signaling pathway and suppressing chondrocyte pyroptosis.
papers.summary: Sinensetin protected human osteoarthritic chondrocytes from IL-1beta-induced viability loss, reducing NLRP3, GSDMD, and ASC expression and pyroptotic markers. Transcriptomics and docking identified SERPINA3 as a candidate target whose knockdown reversed sinensetin's effects. In a rat OA model, sinensetin alleviated pain and cartilage degradation, acting through SERPINA3-mediated NF-kappaB/NLRP3 suppression of chondrocyte pyroptosis.

papers.title: MIF Family Cytokines as Common Mediators of UV-Induced Photocarcinogenesis and Photoaging.
papers.summary: This review examines MIF family cytokines, including MIF and D-DT, as common mediators of UV-induced photocarcinogenesis and photoaging. They promote skin tumor development by enhancing inflammatory responses and suppressing apoptosis of damaged keratinocytes, and contribute to photoaging by regulating matrix metalloproteinase expression, collagen degradation, and extracellular matrix remodeling, positioning them as therapeutic targets for UV damage.
